title: ATM: Why Latent World Models Can Fail to Plan
abstract: arXiv:2606.09028v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Latent world models can achieve accurate latent prediction yet still differ substantially in downstream planning performance. We argue that a key source of this discrepancy lies in the structure of action-induced latent transitions. We formalize action-identifiability through Bayes inverse risk, characterizing how much uncertainty about an action remains after observing the transition it induces. Model-predicted transitions can become highly self-decodable while encoding a domain-specific action relationship that fails to transfer to real environment transitions. We characterize this mismatch through cross-domain inverse transfer, instantiated as the Action-Consistency Transfer Matrix (ATM), a $2\times2$ inverse-risk matrix over real and predicted transition domains. translated_title: ATM：为什么潜在世界模型会规划失败
translated_abstract: 潜在世界模型能够实现准确的潜在预测，但在下游规划性能上却可能存在显著差异。我们认为，造成这一差异的一个关键来源在于动作诱导的潜在转移的结构。我们通过贝叶斯逆风险形式化了动作可辨识性，刻画了在观察到某一动作所诱导的转移之后，关于该动作仍残留多少不确定性。模型预测的转移可以变得高度自可解码，同时却编码了一种特定于领域的动作关系，而这种关系无法迁移到真实环境的转移中。我们通过跨域逆迁移来刻画这种失配，并将其具体化为动作一致性转移矩阵（ATM），即在真实转移域与预测转移域上的一个2×2逆风险矩阵。在TwoRoom、PushT和OGBench-Cube基准上，真实转移的动作可辨识性对下游规划性能的追踪能力显著优于标准预测损失。
tldr: 提出基于贝叶斯逆风险的动作可辨识性概念和动作一致性转移矩阵（ATM），揭示潜在世界模型规划失败的根源：预测转移高度自可解码却编码了无法迁移到真实环境的动作关系，且真实转移的动作可辨识性比标准预测损失更能反映下游规划性能。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces action-identifiability via Bayes inverse risk and the Action-Consistency Transfer Matrix (ATM), revealing that latent world models fail to plan because highly self-decodable predicted transitions encode domain-specific action relationships that fail to transfer to real environment transitions, with true-transition action-identifiability tracking downstream planning far better than standard prediction loss.
